Testing Markdown

Don’t mind just testing out the stuff. Markdown is a simple yet powerful language for formatting text. It’s commonly used for writing documentation, README files, and technical articles. This post will cover how Markdown can be utilized effectively for creating clear and structured documentation.

Contents

  1. Headings and Subheadings
  2. Text Formatting
  3. Code Examples
  4. Ordered and Unordered Lists
  5. Tables and Alignment
  6. Hyperlinks and Images
  7. Blockquotes
  8. Footnotes and References
  9. Mathematical Formulas

Headings and Subheadings

Markdown provides a way to create headings using # symbols. Here’s how you can create various levels of headings:

Main Heading

Secondary Heading

Tertiary Heading

Fourth Level Heading

Fifth Level Heading
Sixth Level Heading

Text Formatting

You can format text in Markdown with various styles:

  • Italic text can be created using single asterisks or underscores.
  • Bold text can be created using double asterisks or double underscores.
  • Strikethrough text uses double tildes.

Code Examples

Highlighting code is straightforward in Markdown. Here are examples for different programming languages:

print(add(5, 3))

Ordered and Unordered Lists

Lists can be created using dashes, asterisks, or numbers:

  • First item
  • Second item
    • Subitem A
    • Subitem B
  1. First ordered item
  2. Second ordered item
  3. Third ordered item

Tables and Alignment

Tables are great for displaying structured data:

Header 1 Header 2 Header 3
Row 1 Data Data
Row 2 Data Data

You can align text in tables using colons:

Left Aligned Center Aligned Right Aligned
Text Text Text

Blockquotes

Blockquotes are used for highlighting quotes:

“Markdown is designed to be easy to write and easy to read.” — John Gruber
